feedback: Written before this candidate has raced; no outcome is stated for it. Iteration 9 (363.7) is the only design that moved the score. Its controller change (base_speed 1.0, kp 2.5, kd 0.4) on the iteration 5 geometry cleared the oval line loss (0.1 per run, 19 of 20 finishes), while the s-bend and slalom still show one line loss per run with max_error at the 0.062 to 0.063 m floor. Iteration 10 (iteration 9 controller with the span widened to ±0.06 m) cut the oval finish rate from 95 to 25 percent and raised steering_oscillation from 0.27 to 0.32, while s-bend line losses fell only from 1.0 to 0.1. The span is therefore not the lever for the score. This candidate keeps your iteration 9 geometry, which is the best-measured platform. The Integrator's controller stays at the iteration 9 values, so the race measures the geometry you proposed. Since this is the final iteration, there is no later race to act on, and the requested changes below are for the record only.
requested_changes: Keep sensor_positions at x = -0.04 to +0.04 with 20 mm pitch and y = 0.04 m. Evidence: iteration 9 (span ±0.04) finished 19 of 20 oval runs, while iteration 10 (span ±0.06) finished 5 of 20 at the same controller.

Keep wheel_track at 0.10 m, wheel_radius at 0.03 m and mass at 0.4 kg. Evidence: these were the iteration 9 values, and no later geometry test (iterations 1, 4, 5, 6) moved max_error or progress off the floor.

Do not widen the span beyond ±0.04 m or move y away from 0.04 m without new race evidence. Evidence: the ±0.06 m span (iteration 10) cut the oval finish rate and raised steering_oscillation, and lead changes (iteration 7, y = 0.06 m) gave no line-loss gain.
